semantic_mapping.rationale: BUILD-G01 deliberately replaces clean-before-write reference publication. Current generate assembles all expected files in memory then publishOwnedFiles stages/verifies bytes and removes stale owned targets only during controlled promotion. Thus the specific old deletion-before-writing state is retired; successful stale cleanup remains implemented.

BUILD-G01 deliberately replaces unconditional partial-output-on-error within reference publication. Render errors occur before publication; publisher failure rolls applied files back or retains an explicit unusable marker/journal if recovery fails. Other later CLI owners can already have published, so no global transaction or whole-tree rollback is claimed.

BUILD-G01 deliberately replaces Academy-root deletion before rendering. Current code constructs every Academy route/generated projection in memory before owned staged publication. Stale owned files are removed only in the promotion transaction; the old output-removed-first intermediate state is retired.

BUILD-G01 deliberately replaces late Academy render failure leaving an incomplete tree. Action/render errors precede the publisher. Publication failure restores the old projection or retains an unusable marker/journal if rollback fails. This does not certify all consumers/global output trees or an executed crash journey.

rationale: Maintained BUILD-G01 explicitly requires staging/validation before replacement and old-complete or unusable outcome on failure, superseding the four named baseline delete-first/unconditionally-partial intermediate states. Successful ownership-safe generation remains required.
limits: Only finite conditional source control-flow clauses. No new runtime/browser/build/corpus/installed/whole-machine/task/program acceptance.
Every frozen cited source path is bound, with logic witnesses separate from broader family citation exposure.
Metadata and unrelated staged cancellation changes are outside these inputs. Source epoch is immutable483d; no claim the whole worktree was clean.
